To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the flowfield in a thin channel between a porous plate with fluid injection through it and a parallel imper- meable plate is described by an integral equation for the Mach number.

the inviscid compressible flow between a porous wall and a parallel imper- meable wall is described by the solution of a Fredholm integral equation of the second kind, which can be solved numerically for arbitrary values of the Mach number, the ratio of specific heats, the injection velocity, and the ratio of the injection distance to the lateral dimension of the plates.
the flow is choked in the vicinity of a critical lateral extent of the channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical analysis of compressibility effects in thin counterflowing streams.
the analysis of the invi- sible, high Reynolds number flow between a porous and an impermeable plate, in the presence of uniform fluid injection through the porous plate.
the analysis of flows between two porous plates at large Reynolds num- bers and with the effects of compressibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the present study, when combined with the results of the previous studies, provide a complete theoretical analysis of the flow in the inviscid region between porous plates, including the effects of compressibility.

the results of the present study are needed for providing external boundary-layer boundary conditions for studying the viscous and chemically reacting flow between two counterflow- ing streams when compressibility effects are important, as is the case in supersonic combustion in turbulent mixing flows.
the results presented herein, in conjunction with those of Refs. 2 and 3, should provide the necessary external-flow conditions for studying the viscous layer in counterflow diffusion flames.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the problem of Proudman,1 with the addition of heat transfer and combustion, for the case of large Reynolds numbers and compressible flow, for both plane and axisymmetric flows.

the flowfield between a porous plate (the injection surface) and a parallel imper- meable plate (the stagnation surface) is analyzed for small values of a dimensionless separation distance, defined by the ratio of the injection- stagnation separation distance to the width of the injection surface.
the flow between two parallel plates is considered in which one of the plates is porous and the fluid is injected into the flow from the porous wall.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of a porous plate, there is a choking limit for the flow, which occurs at a critical value for the lateral extent of that plate.
the flow between a plate and a counter-flowing plate is compressible.
compressibility effects can be important in the inviscid region of counterflow diffusion flames.
